name: Pro-Europeanism
summary: Pro-Europeanism favours European integration and EU membership, holding that pooling sovereignty in shared institutions secures peace, prosperity and common values for European states. Its own foundational texts (the Schuman Declaration, the Treaties and the Charter of Fundamental Rights) settle positions on democracy, the rule of law, rights, a social market economy, the euro and mutual defence, but not on most economic, social or cultural questions, where pro-European parties differ. Scholars classify pro-European attitudes as enthusiast, equivocal or critical.

tried.how: searched for a copy of the Manifesto hosted elsewhere; none opened

scope: The mainstream pro-European outlook as set out in the founding texts that define the project (the Schuman Declaration of 1950, the Treaty on European Union, the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the Charter of Fundamental Rights, which the Treaties tie to the Union's aims) and in the scholarship on what being pro-European means (Ostrowski 2023 on Europeanism, which Wikidata lists as another name for it). Positions of individual parties, party families (EPP, Renew, S&D, Greens/EFA) or national governments are other subjects and do not answer here, nor do Euroscepticism or non-EU pan-European projects. Where the sources do not state a position, the answer is null.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Article 13 TEU makes the European Central Bank one of the Union's institutions and Article 3(4) sets up a monetary union, which a free market in money would replace.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Article 14(1) TEU has the European Parliament exercise budgetary functions jointly with the Council.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Article 10 TEU founds the Union on representative democracy, with political parties at Union level contributing to political awareness and the will of citizens.

clerical-rule.rationale: Article 2 TEU founds the Union on democracy and the rule of law, which rule by senior religious scholars as the highest authority contradicts.

collective-defense.rationale: Article 42(7) TEU says if a Member State is the victim of armed aggression the others owe it aid and assistance by all means in their power.

common-currency.rationale: Article 3(4) TEU says the Union shall establish an economic and monetary union whose currency is the euro.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Article 2 TEU founds the Union on the rule of law and respect for human rights, including those of minorities, which limit what a national majority may decide.

decide-locally.rationale: The TEU preamble and Article 1 say decisions are taken as closely as possible to the citizen, and Article 5 applies subsidiarity.

delink-world-market.rationale: Article 3(5) TEU commits the Union to contribute to free and fair trade and to solidarity and mutual respect among peoples, which ending economic ties would reverse.

democracy-best.rationale: Article 2 TEU founds the Union on democracy and Article 10 on representative democracy, and Article 21 has it advance democracy in the wider world.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Article 2 and Article 3(3) TEU name equality between women and men as a value the Union promotes, which different public roles by sex contradict.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Article 42(7) TEU binds Member States to mutual defence, and Article 42(2) treats NATO commitments as the foundation of collective defence.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Article 6(1) TEU gives the Charter of Fundamental Rights the same legal value as the Treaties, so the Union's institutions are bound by a rights text that ordinary legislation cannot amend.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Article 2 TEU names equality and non-discrimination among the Union's founding values.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Article 3(3) TEU has the Union combat discrimination and Article 2 names non-discrimination as a value.

future-generations.rationale: Article 3(3) TEU names solidarity between generations and the sustainable development of Europe and Article 3(5) of the Earth.

minority-language-support.rationale: Article 3(3) TEU says the Union shall respect its rich cultural and linguistic diversity, and Article 2 names the rights of persons belonging to minorities.

nation-first.rationale: Article 21 TEU commits the Union to promote multilateral solutions to common problems and Article 3(5) to solidarity and mutual respect among peoples.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Article 3(5) TEU commits the Union to strict observance and development of international law.

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 2 TEU names democracy and pluralism as Union values, and Article 10(4) gives political parties at Union level a role in expressing citizens' will.

open-government-data.rationale: Article 1 TEU says decisions are taken as openly as possible and as closely as possible to the citizen, and Article 10(3) says decisions are taken openly.

organic-representation.rationale: Article 10 TEU founds the Union on representative democracy and names political parties as the vehicle for expressing citizens' will.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Article 2 TEU founds the Union on democracy and the rule of law, which rule resting on personal oaths of loyalty contradicts.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The TEU preamble resolves to continue an ever closer union among the peoples of Europe, and Article 1 has the Member States confer competences on the Union to attain their common objectives.

population-transfer.rationale: Article 2 TEU names respect for human rights, including those of persons belonging to minorities, and non-discrimination as common values, which expelling a minority contradicts.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Article 3(3) TEU says the Union shall ensure that Europe's cultural heritage is safeguarded and enhanced.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Article 21 TEU says the Union's external action seeks to advance democracy, the rule of law and human rights in the wider world.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Article 2 TEU founds the Union on the rule of law, which means rulers govern under established public law.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Article 2 TEU names non-discrimination as a value common to Union and Member States, and Article 3(3) has the Union combat discrimination.

racial-franchise.rationale: Article 2 TEU founds the Union on democracy and equality and names non-discrimination as a value, which restricting the vote to one ethnic group contradicts.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 2 TEU names non-discrimination and equality as values and Article 3(3) has the Union combat social exclusion and discrimination, which legal segregation contradicts.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Article 2 TEU names respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities, and non-discrimination as values, which removing an ethnic group contradicts.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Article 3(5) TEU lists the eradication of poverty and solidarity among peoples among the Union's aims in the wider world.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Article 3(3) TEU says the Union shall ensure that Europe's cultural heritage is safeguarded and enhanced.

separated-powers.rationale: Article 13(2) TEU has each Union institution act only within the limits of the powers the Treaties confer on it, and Article 2 founds the Union on the rule of law.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Article 2 and Article 3(3) TEU name equality between women and men as a value the Union promotes.

social-market-economy.rationale: Article 3(3) TEU states the Union works for a highly competitive social market economy aiming at full employment and social progress, and combats social exclusion.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Article 2 TEU founds the Union on the rule of law, which a ruler above the law contradicts.

state-harmful.rationale: The Union is a union of states whose essential State functions Article 4(2) TEU requires it to respect, and the Charter's rights bind the state rather than abolish it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Article 2 TEU names democracy, pluralism and tolerance as values common to the Member States and Article 10 founds the Union on representative democracy.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Article 3(5) TEU commits the Union to contribute to free and fair trade among its aims in the wider world.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Article 3(5) and Article 21 TEU commit the Union to peace and the principles of the UN Charter.

total-state.rationale: Article 2 TEU founds the Union on human dignity, freedom, democracy and respect for human rights, which a state directing every area of life contradicts.

women-suffrage.rationale: Article 2 TEU names equality between women and men as a value that prevails in the Union and Article 3(3) has the Union promote it, so women's political rights equal to men's are part of it.

missingStatements.text: A single currency shared by several countries is better than separate national currencies.
missingStatements.rationale: Economic and monetary union with the euro is a stated aim of the EU and a central pro-European policy.

missingStatements.text: People should be free to live, work and study in any country of a continental union without a visa.
missingStatements.rationale: Freedom of movement without internal borders is an explicit EU aim and defining pro-European benefit.
missingStatements.declined: Free movement is covered loosely by open-borders and pool-sovereignty; too specific to one union.

missingStatements.text: Democratic countries that meet shared standards should be able to join a union of states as new members.
missingStatements.rationale: Schuman's High Authority was open to other European countries and the EU is open to further members.
missingStatements.declined: Enlargement of one union; covered by pool-sovereignty.

missingStatements.text: A united Europe should become a federation.
missingStatements.rationale: Schuman described the coal and steel community as a first step toward a European federation, though adherents split on how far to go.

notes: Pro-Europeans disagree among themselves on federalism versus intergovernmental cooperation, fiscal rules, migration and enlargement; positions that only a party family holds are not the ideology's and are null. Earlier answers resting on what a typical centrist pro-European holds were nulled in this pass. Themes searched in the Treaties, the Charter, the Schuman Declaration, EU aims pages and scholarship: economy and money, trade, government and democracy, rights, religion, gender, culture, environment, defence and external action; the economic, social and culture-war themes are largely silent. The Ventotene Manifesto (europarl.europa.eu) refused scripted access (403) and Churchill's Zurich speech was not available as full text.
